persona.title: Who is your assistant?
persona.description: Choose how the assistant introduces itself and how it sounds. Everything except the name is optional, and you can change it later.

data_description.agent_name: How the name is written, for example N.O.V.A.
data_description.spoken_name: How it is said, for example Nova. Leave empty if it is the same as the name.
data_description.acronym_expansion: Only if the name is an acronym.
data_description.owner: A person or household, for example the Smiths.
data_description.purpose: One sentence about what the assistant is for.
data_description.personality: Changes the wording of answers. It never changes what the assistant does.
data_description.traits: Free text that steers the tone of open conversation, for example: curious, loves astronomy.

primary.title: Language model
primary.description: An optional language model helps with unusual phrasing and open conversation. Commands and questions about your home work without one. Choose where it runs.

data_description.url: Leave empty for the default of the chosen provider.

fallback.title: Fallback language model
fallback.description: Optional. Used only if the first language model fails, for example a hosted service as a backup for a local model. Choose none to skip.

feeds.title: News and status feeds
feeds.description: Optional, and you can add feeds later. Give each feed a name you would say, and its address. Ask by name: "what's new in sports", "anything on spaceflight", "is GitHub down". "What's the news" reads the feeds with news in their name. Any name works. Leave a pair empty to skip it. Two empty pairs are always added when you come back, up to 20 feeds. Feed text is only read out, never treated as a command.

data_description.name_4: Anything you like: Local news, Spaceflight, Tech, a status page...
data_description.url_1: The RSS or Atom address, usually ending in /rss, /feed or .xml.
data_description.feed_summary: Off: the headlines are read, and you get a summary only when you ask for one, for example "summarize the news". Summaries need a language model. If a summary names anything the feed doesn't say, the headlines are read instead, but small models can still change what a story means.
data_description.feed_count: How many items to read or summarize per answer.
data_description.feed_entities: Only if you already use Feedparser or Feed Reader. Neither is required.

error.cannot_connect: Could not reach the server. Check the address and that the server is running.
error.feed_failed: This address could not be read as an RSS or Atom feed.
error.feed_missing: Add the feed's address, or clear the name.
error.feed_duplicate: Another feed already has this name.

data.confirm_sensitive: Ask before unlocking, disarming or opening garage doors
data.strip_assistant_name: Ignore the assistant's name at the start or end of a request
data.ha_fallback: Let Home Assistant's own Assist handle what this assistant doesn't (timers, lists, your custom sentences)
data.home_chat: Let the language model answer questions about the home (larger models only; small ones make things up)

data_description.weather_entity: Optional. Used for "what's the weather". Left empty, the first available weather entity is used.
